Home, The What Needs You Panel. From “What Needs You”.

What Needs You is where the world tells you things and asks you things. A notice says what happened: groceries you couldn’t pay for, a commitment you slept through, a welcome to the school. A question carries its answers as buttons, such as File It or Keep The Account, and Dismiss. The number beside Home on the menu is how many of both are waiting.

How This Works

RBC Signature No Limit Banking at RBC Royal Bank, C$26,489. Primary.

Your wages and other payments are paid into it. Your everyday card’s autopay pays from it.

The primary account is where your debit card’s everyday purchases come from it; cash from a machine comes out of it; bills you pay by hand come from it; a new standing order or autopay starts from it. Making another primary moves nothing already set up.

How This Works

Wages and other payments go to RBC Signature No Limit Banking: a change reaches Yale’s payroll in 7 days, about one of its weekly pay cycles, as Yale says, and other payers in 14, SLATE’s estimate (employers say one to two pay cycles).

How This Works
Open An Account At Another Bank
How This Works

There’s no switching service here. To move banks: open the account, have your wages paid into it, move each standing order and autopay, move the money across, then close the old account. The new account starts with nothing, and its own history.

Scotiabank

Apply

It opens the account as you apply. SLATE has found no opening deposit it asks for. The debit card takes 7 business days, as the bank’s replacement card does: SLATE’s estimate, as no figure for a new account’s card was found. Money between banks here takes 1 business day, by electronic funds transfer. Its TD Unlimited Chequing costs C$17.95 a month, waived with keeping C$4,000.00 in it all month.

Sources And Estimates

12 months at 2.45%

How This Works

Locked for 12 months at a fixed 2.45%. At its end it renews for the same term at the bank’s rate on the day, unless you choose another way the bank allows. Breaking one early, where the bank lets you, is under Your Accounts Over Time.

RBC cancels a lost or stolen debit card and issues a new one, and blocks a lost or stolen credit card from further use and issues a new card. The first debit card replacement in a calendar year is free and each further one costs $5.00, unless the replacement is due to fraud, a name change, or a card that arrived damaged.

RBC texts the credit cardholder from short code 722373 or 347722 asking them to reply Y to confirm a transaction or N if they don't recognize it, after which a fraud specialist contacts them. The card agreement says RBC can block the card without telling the customer when it suspects fraudulent use.

The law, for the debit card: Debit cards fall under the voluntary Canadian Code of Practice for Consumer Debit Card Services (section 5): the cardholder isn't liable for losses from circumstances beyond their control, including being the victim of fraud, theft or coercion, technical failures, and use after the card is reported lost or stolen. A cardholder who contributed (for example by voluntarily sharing a PIN or not reporting in reasonable time) can be liable, but no more than the card's withdrawal limits, and more only where overdraft or a linked credit line is attached. There’s no statutory dollar cap for debit.

For the credit card: Bank Act, S.C. 1991, c. 46, s. 627.33: a borrower's maximum liability for unauthorized use of a credit card issued in Canada is $50 unless they showed gross negligence (gross fault in Quebec), and nothing after they report the card lost, stolen or at risk. Use of the PIN alone doesn't prove gross negligence. For non-bank federally regulated issuers, FCAC says the cap is the lesser of $50 or the agreement's amount.

A payment reported as not yours: Debit Card Code of Practice: the issuer must respond to a report of an unauthorized transaction as soon as possible and in no more than 10 business days, a limit it can pause while waiting for a signed statement or affidavit. No statutory refund deadline is set for credit cards.

The Marketplace

In New York, Los Angeles or New Haven

How This Works

You can enroll in public cover or the marketplace only while you live in New York, Los Angeles or New Haven. On a low month’s income, Medicaid (Medi-Cal in California, HUSKY D in Connecticut) takes you at 138% of the poverty line, in New York the Essential Plan to 200%, and in Connecticut Covered Connecticut to 175% of the year before’s, at any time and with no premium; Covered Connecticut is for an income over HUSKY D’s line, whatever your status, and comes with the premium tax credit, from 100% of the poverty line; from 2027 a student in F-1 status or a graduate on OPT has none. From 2027 Medicaid’s work rules are met by a month you spend any of at the School, or one with C$794.60 of income (pay, interest, a benefit or a pension): in Connecticut the month before you apply, and any one of the 6 months before a renewal. Being 65 or over, SNAP received under its work rules, or a stay in hospital you ask for counts as meeting them. Short of it, a notice gives 30 days from its receipt to answer before an application is denied or cover ends, and an ending is said 10 days or more ahead, at a month’s end. You pay the whole premium each month, and the return gives back what’s over your share of income, a nonresident’s 1040-NR too: none over 400% of the poverty line, since the enhanced credits ended with 2025.
